# Capabilities and caveats

<!-- Generated by internal/apidoc from the packages' doc comments: edit those, then run `task docs:api`. -->

What a capability is and carries: its principal, its caveats, its amounts and ceilings, and the checks an operation is held to. Part of the [API reference](README.md).

|---|---|
| [`github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes`](#limes) | 24 declarations |

<a id="limes"></a><a id="package-limes"></a>

## Package limes

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes"`

Package limes is an object-capability authorisation primitive designed for agentic workloads.

A Capability is a short-lived, signed token granting its bearer a specific set of operations on a specific set of resources, with explicit budget and lifetime caveats. It is delegable — a parent issues a strictly narrower child to a sub-agent — and individually revocable. Compared with long-lived API keys or role-based access it gives:

  - Per-call attribution: every call carries the capability ID, so audit and cost roll up by it, down to which run of which agent spent what.
  - Budget enforcement at the authorisation boundary: the meter ([github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/meter](metering.md#package-meter)) refuses a charge once a ceiling is exhausted, rather than business logic discovering it three calls deep.
  - Mid-flight revocation: a compromised agent's capability is revoked, together with everything it delegated.
  - Sub-capabilities without an operator: an orchestrator narrows its own authority for each sub-agent it spawns, through the Issuer with no admin API in the path, or offline as a Biscuit block with no call at all.

Wire format is JWT compact serialization with Ed25519 signatures (\`alg: Ed25519\`, RFC 9864, or \`EdDSA\` where SignerConfig.Algorithm asks for it), or a Biscuit v3 sealing such a token; docs/standards.md lists every standard followed. Verification is local: the signature is checked against a resolved public key, and the store reads, whether the capability is revoked and, for a Biscuit, whether its copy is, go through one short-lived cache ([RevocationCache](revocation.md#limes.RevocationCache)), so consumers scale horizontally without contending on a shared store.

#### Packages

Two standards the verifier relies on are packages of their own, usable without the rest: [github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/jwks](keys.md#package-jwks) for key sets (RFC 7517) and [github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/dpop](dpop.md#package-dpop) for proof of possession (RFC 9449). [github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/meter](metering.md#package-meter) counts requests and spend against a capability's ceilings and keeps the charges ledger; a consumer that only verifies tokens never imports it. [github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/inspect](inspection.md#package-inspect) reads a token without verifying it, for tooling. limestest holds a consumer's mapping of the error codes to the ones it was written against. memstore, storetest and metertest serve stores; dpop/dpoptest and jwks/jwkstest check a replay cache, a nonce source and a key resolver. Modules of their own carry what the root module does not resolve: github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/pgstore, every store contract over PostgreSQL; github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/redisreplay, a replay cache over Redis; github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/otelmetric, OpenTelemetry instruments; github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/exchange, OAuth 2.0 token exchange (RFC 8693); and github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/biscuit, the Biscuit form.

#### What you implement

Three contracts are required; a consumer that implements them needs nothing else:

  - [Store](storage.md#limes.Store) — capability records and revocations; an [Issuer](issuing.md#limes.Issuer) needs only its [IssuanceStore](storage.md#limes.IssuanceStore) half, a [Revoker](revocation.md#limes.Revoker) only its [RevocationStore](storage.md#limes.RevocationStore) one. IsRevoked answers for the capability's whole delegation chain, at most [MaxDelegationDepth](storage.md#limes.MaxDelegationDepth) ancestors deep. No transactions required; an in-memory map is a valid implementation. A store that scopes calls to a tenant refuses one whose request names another with [ErrScopeMismatch](errors.md#limes.ErrScopeMismatch). A store paired with a meter.TenantUsageEraser refuses Insert for a tenant whose usage was erased with [ErrTenantErased](errors.md#limes.ErrTenantErased), which the [Issuer](issuing.md#limes.Issuer) answers as [ErrTenantGone](errors.md#limes.ErrTenantGone).
  - [github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/meter.UsageStore](metering.md#meter.UsageStore) — request and spend counters and the charges ledger, for a consumer that meters; see package meter.
  - [KeyResolver](verifying.md#limes.KeyResolver) — public verification keys. [jwks.Static](keys.md#jwks.Static) ships as a working implementation and supports rotation via SetKey / RemoveKey; [jwks.Remote](keys.md#jwks.Remote) fetches an issuer's JWKS for verifiers that run apart from it.

More are needed only with the feature they serve: [RevocationLineageLookup](revocation.md#limes.RevocationLineageLookup) for a [RevocationCache](revocation.md#limes.RevocationCache) to drop only what a revocation outdates, [BiscuitRevocationLookup](revocation.md#limes.BiscuitRevocationLookup) to accept Biscuit tokens and [BiscuitRevocationStore](revocation.md#limes.BiscuitRevocationStore) to revoke one copy of one, [RecordCensus](storage.md#limes.RecordCensus) to count capability records by disposition across tenants, [RecordLister](storage.md#limes.RecordLister) to list a tenant's records with their dispositions and [RecordListingReader](storage.md#limes.RecordListingReader) to read one with its disposition — [RecordReporter](storage.md#limes.RecordReporter) is both, and the Census that memstore.NewCensus and pgstore.NewCensus return serves all three — [BulkRevoker](revocation.md#limes.BulkRevoker) to revoke by user, client, identity-provider session or agent run (meter.MatchingReleaser frees the holds it stopped), [ExchangeStore](storage.md#limes.ExchangeStore) to exchange each subject token for one capability, [TenantRecordEraser](storage.md#limes.TenantRecordEraser) to remove a tenant, [dpop.ReplayCache](dpop.md#dpop.ReplayCache) to share DPoP replay state across replicas ([dpop.MemoryReplayCache](dpop.md#dpop.MemoryReplayCache) ships for one process), and [dpop.Nonces](dpop.md#dpop.Nonces) to require server nonces ([dpop.HMACNonces](dpop.md#dpop.HMACNonces) ships, and works across replicas holding the same keys).

A Capability crosses the API by value, in and out: no caller can alter one another holds, and one that is not there is an error, never nil.

Every amount is [Nanos](#limes.Nanos), an int64 count of billionths of the unit (BudgetCeiling.UnitCode, an ISO 4217 code; XXX for a budget that is not money), so spend sums, compares and refunds exactly, with no rounding left to the consumer.

Every read names what it reads — Store.GetRecord a capability, meter.MeterReader.GetUsage the counters — so one type may implement Store and meter.UsageStore together, or each apart as memstore does.

#### Guarantees

Rejections are matchable sentinels, so a consumer can map each to its own transport status, or let Verifier.ErrorResponse map it to HTTP. Every error the package returns has a stable [Code](errors.md#limes.Code) ([CodeOf](errors.md#limes.CodeOf)), and [ProblemOf](errors.md#limes.ProblemOf) builds its RFC 9457 body for an API that is not a protected resource; never match an error's text. A charge rejected by any ceiling — a Biscuit copy's, the capability's, an ancestor's, the tenant's — leaves every counter and the ledger unmutated, so retrying after a rejection is safe. Delegation needs [OpShare](#limes.OpShare) on the parent and can only narrow: any widening returns [ErrDelegationTooWide](errors.md#limes.ErrDelegationTooWide), and a differing unit code returns [ErrUnitCodeMismatch](errors.md#limes.ErrUnitCodeMismatch) rather than converting.

#### Enforcing caveats

[Caveats.Check](#limes.Caveats.Check) and [Caveats.CheckSource](#limes.Caveats.CheckSource) are the single definition of what the caveats mean at use time; delegation narrowing ([Narrows](#limes.Narrows)) uses the same resource matcher ([MatchResource](#limes.MatchResource)), so the two cannot disagree.

See README.md for a five-minute walkthrough and examples/quickstart for it as a runnable program.

<sub>[check.go](../../check.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrEffectConflict"></a>

### limes.ErrEffectConflict

```go
var ErrEffectConflict error = &familyError{"limes: declared effect conflicts with the operation", ErrInvalidRequest}
```

ErrEffectConflict is a declared effect that contradicts a built-in operation's own ("put" declared a read), or one this package does not define. A declaration may name a built-in operation's effect, never change it: a write declared a read would shed IdempotencyKeyRequired. It is a programming error in the consumer, so it matches ErrInvalidRequest.

<sub>[effect.go](../../effect.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrInvalidCaveats"></a>

### limes.ErrInvalidCaveats

```go
var ErrInvalidCaveats error = &familyError{"limes: invalid caveats", ErrInvalidRequest}
```

ErrInvalidCaveats is returned when a caveat bag is malformed: a budget outside 0..MaxNanos, a request limit outside 0..MaxIJSONInteger, an unknown unit, an empty resource entry, an unparsable CIDR, an operation name that is not well formed. It is a request error, not an authorisation decision — the capability was never minted — so it also matches ErrInvalidRequest.

<sub>[wire.go](../../wire.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MatchResource"></a>

### limes.MatchResource

```go
func MatchResource(prefix, uri string) bool
```

MatchResource reports whether uri falls under prefix, matched at a path- segment boundary: "corpus/public" covers "corpus/public" and "corpus/public/x", but not "corpus/public-secret". A prefix that already ends in "/" matches anything beneath it. An empty prefix matches nothing — a caveat that means "everything" is written by leaving the list empty, not by an empty entry, so a stray "" can never silently widen a capability.

A uri with a dot segment — "." or "..", percent-encoded or not, between slashes that may be encoded or backslashes — matches nothing: what it names depends on how the consumer resolves it, so the match it seems to make by its text proves nothing about where it leads. That covers a consumer that percent-decodes at most twice before it resolves the path, and no other notation: one that decodes more often, or whose backend resolves Unicode look-alikes (U+FF0E), overlong UTF-8 (%c0%ae), %u escapes or trailing dots and spaces as a dot segment, canonicalises the resource itself before it asks.

This is the single definition of a resource match. Delegation narrowing and request-time enforcement both go through it, so the two can never disagree about what a prefix reaches.

<sub>[resource.go](../../resource.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MatchResourceName"></a>

### limes.MatchResourceName

```go
func MatchResourceName(prefix, uri string) bool
```

MatchResourceName reports whether uri starts with prefix, as strings and across segments: "drafts/billing-" covers "drafts/billing-q3" and "drafts/billing-q3/notes", but not "drafts/billing". Like MatchResource, an empty prefix matches nothing, and neither does a uri with a dot segment. It is the single definition of a name-prefix match, for requests and for delegation alike.

<sub>[resource.go](../../resource.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Narrows"></a>

### limes.Narrows

```go
func Narrows(parent, child Capability) error
```

Narrows returns nil when child is a narrowing of parent: the same tenant; an audience that is a subset; a validity window that starts no earlier and ends no later; a key binding when parent has one; every operation allowed by parent; every resource and source IP reachable by parent; request, copy and budget ceilings no larger; tainted reads no broader; and an idempotency key required when parent requires one. A widening is ErrDelegationTooWide; a budget in another unit than parent's, unless it spends nothing and names none, is ErrUnitCodeMismatch. Issuer.Delegate runs this check before signing the child token, so a misuse fails at issue time, not later.

The function is exposed at package level so external tooling can dry-run a delegation without going through the issuer.

<a id="limes.AgentPrincipal"></a>

### limes.AgentPrincipal

```go
type AgentPrincipal struct {
	// AgentType is a human-meaningful label ("research-orchestrator",
	// "code-reviewer-bot"). Used for grouping, dashboards, anomaly
	// baselines.
	AgentType string
	// AgentVersion pins the build / git-sha of the agent runtime.
	AgentVersion string
	// RunID is a UUID minted by the agent host at session start.
	RunID uuid.UUID
	// ParentRunID is the RunID of the agent whose capability this one was
	// delegated from. Issuer.Delegate sets it from the parent, and refuses
	// a request naming another; zero for a root capability, or one
	// delegated from a principal that is no agent or names no run.
	ParentRunID uuid.UUID
	// Model identifies the LLM behind the agent ("example-model-1",
	// "gpt-5-pro"). Used for cost attribution.
	Model string
	// MCPClient is the agent host's user-agent ("example-host@1.4.0",
	// "cursor@0.44"). Useful for compatibility tracking.
	MCPClient string
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

AgentPrincipal carries the fields specific to AI-agent principals, for audit and lineage: per-tool-call replay reconstructs the call graph from them.

<sub>[principal.go](../../principal.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.BudgetCeiling"></a>

### limes.BudgetCeiling

```go
type BudgetCeiling struct {
	// Max is the most that may be spent; 0 allows nothing. Within
	// 0..MaxNanos, and 0 when Unlimited.
	Max Nanos
	// Unlimited lifts the ceiling.
	Unlimited bool
	// UnitCode is the unit Max counts in: an ISO 4217 code (IsUnitCode),
	// AbstractUnitCode for a budget that is not money. Required when the
	// ceiling lets anything be spent; may be empty on the zero ceiling.
	UnitCode string
}
```

BudgetCeiling bounds an amount spent: at most Max of UnitCode, or any amount of it when Unlimited. The unit is part of the bound, as a currency is part of an amount: a ceiling that lets anything be spent names what, and the zero ceiling, which lets nothing be, needs none.


Within reports whether c allows no more than outer, by amount alone: whether the two count in one unit is the caller's to check, and to refuse as ErrUnitCodeMismatch rather than as a wider ceiling.

<a id="limes.Capability"></a>

### limes.Capability

```go
type Capability struct {
	// ID is the unique identifier (UUIDv7 — sortable by issuance time
	// so per-tenant indexes stay tight).
	ID uuid.UUID

	// Issuer is the service instance that minted the capability. Verifiers
	// accept tokens whose Issuer is in the trusted set.
	Issuer string

	// Subject is the principal the capability authorises.
	Subject Principal

	// Audience pins which services the capability is valid for: a
	// verifier refuses a token whose audience does not include the one it
	// verifies for (VerifyRequest.Audience).
	Audience []string

	// Caveats is the conjunction of restrictions — every caveat must
	// be satisfied by the request, and child capabilities can only
	// add further caveats, never relax one.
	Caveats Caveats

	// IssuedAt / NotBefore / ExpiresAt are standard JWT-style times.
	IssuedAt  time.Time
	NotBefore time.Time
	ExpiresAt time.Time

	// ParentID, if non-zero, points at the parent capability whose
	// holder delegated this one. Narrowing is checked once, at
	// delegation. At use, the lineage matters twice: revoking any
	// ancestor revokes this capability (Store.IsRevoked answers for the
	// whole chain), and every charge also debits each ancestor, so a
	// parent's budget bounds the spend of everything delegated from it.
	ParentID uuid.UUID

	// ConfirmationJKT, when set, binds the capability to a key: the RFC 7638
	// thumbprint of the public key whose holder alone may present it. Every
	// request must then carry a DPoP proof signed by that key (package dpop). A
	// delegated child of a bound capability is bound too. Carried in the
	// token as `cnf.jkt`, and absent from tokens that are not bound.
	ConfirmationJKT string

	// ClientID is the OAuth client the capability was granted to: the
	// client of the access token it was exchanged for, or the software its
	// subject runs as. Carried as RFC 9068's client_id, which the profile
	// makes required. It describes the grant and restricts nothing.
	ClientID string

	// OnBehalfOf is the principal on whose behalf Subject acts, when it acts
	// for another: the user an agent works for, as the identity provider
	// names them. A delegated child keeps its parent's or, when the parent
	// has none, acts on behalf of the parent's holder. In the token it is
	// sub, with Subject as act (RFC 8693 §4.1). It describes the grant and
	// restricts nothing: Subject is who the capability authorises.
	OnBehalfOf *Principal

	// PriorActors are the subjects of the holders this capability was
	// delegated through on behalf of OnBehalfOf, nearest first: the token's
	// nested act. Empty for a capability issued rather
	// than delegated, and for a child of a capability with no OnBehalfOf.
	PriorActors []string
}
```

Capability is the in-memory representation of a token. The wire form is a JWT; this struct is what the Issuer fills before signing, and what Verifier.Verify returns inside a VerifiedCapability.

<a id="limes.Caveats"></a>

### limes.Caveats

```go
type Caveats struct {
	// Ops is the set of operations the capability authorises. The
	// issuer rejects an empty set: a capability that allows nothing is
	// a mistake, not a credential.
	Ops []Op

	// ResourcePrefixes restricts the capability to URIs under any prefix
	// in the slice, matched at a "/" segment boundary (MatchResource):
	// "a/b" covers "a/b" and "a/b/c" but not "a/bc". Empty slice =
	// unrestricted within the tenant; an empty ENTRY is invalid.
	ResourcePrefixes []string

	// ResourceURIs pins the capability to specific URIs. Used by
	// hand-off flows where the parent passes exactly the artifacts the
	// child needs.
	ResourceURIs []string

	// ResourceNamePrefixes restricts the capability to URIs that start with
	// any entry, as strings (MatchResourceName): "drafts/billing-" covers
	// "drafts/billing-q3" and "drafts/billing-q3/notes", where a
	// ResourcePrefixes entry covers whole segments alone. An empty entry is
	// invalid.
	ResourceNamePrefixes []string

	// Requests caps the total number of times the capability may be
	// used within its TTL; the zero value allows none, and
	// RequestCeiling{Unlimited: true} lifts the cap.
	Requests RequestCeiling

	// Budget is the cost budget the capability authorises, exact to the
	// nano, in Budget.UnitCode — the unit every amount metered against the
	// capability counts in. The zero value allows no spend and needs no
	// unit: the capability counts requests (meter.RequestCounter.Bump) but
	// no amount, and a Charge, Reserve or Settle on it with no unit is
	// ErrInvalidRequest.
	// BudgetCeiling{Unlimited: true, UnitCode: u} lifts the bound. Once it
	// is exhausted, a charge returns ErrBudgetExceeded. A delegated child
	// whose budget names no unit takes its parent's.
	Budget BudgetCeiling

	// Copies is how many Biscuit copies of the capability a meter counts —
	// the copies whose blocks set request or budget limits of their own,
	// each a counter the store keeps; the zero value counts none, and
	// CopyQuota{Unlimited: true} as many as the store allows. A block that
	// sets no limit makes no copy a meter counts, so it needs none.
	Copies CopyQuota

	// AllowTaintedRead permits non-mutating operations on resources the
	// consumer has flagged with prompt-injection / PII / secrets signals.
	// Off by default. Enforced by Caveats.Check, which can only act on a
	// taint signal the consumer supplies in CheckRequest.ResourceTainted
	// — a consumer that tracks no taint flags gets no protection from
	// this caveat, and should say so rather than imply it.
	AllowTaintedRead bool

	// IdempotencyKeyRequired forces the bearer to send an explicit
	// idempotency key on mutating operations (CheckRequest.Mutating).
	// Enforced by Caveats.Check from CheckRequest.HasIdempotencyKey.
	IdempotencyKeyRequired bool

	// SourceIPCIDR optionally pins the capability to clients whose
	// observed IP is in the listed CIDRs. Empty = unconstrained.
	// Enforced by Caveats.CheckSource; delegation requires each child
	// network to lie inside a parent network.
	SourceIPCIDR []string
}
```

Caveats is a typed bag of restrictions, AND-combined. Ops is required; an empty resource or source-network list places no restriction on its axis. The ceilings are explicit: a zero RequestCeiling or BudgetCeiling allows nothing, and only Unlimited lifts one.

It is written into a token as the limes\_caveats claim (wire.go), so renaming a field changes nothing a token carries. A verifier refuses a member it does not know: a caveat it cannot enforce must not pass as one it did.

A child capability may only narrow caveats — set a tighter prefix, drop ops, lower the budget, shorten TTL. Issuer.Delegate enforces this through Narrows before it signs, and the verifier does for every Biscuit attenuation block, so an attempt to widen is refused, never minted.

<sub>[types.go](../../types.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Caveats.AllowsResource"></a>

#### limes.Caveats.AllowsResource

```go
func (c Caveats) AllowsResource(uri string) bool
```

AllowsResource reports whether uri is reachable under the resource caveats: unrestricted caveats allow any uri; restricted ones require an exact ResourceURIs entry, a covering ResourcePrefixes entry (MatchResource) or a ResourceNamePrefixes entry it starts with (MatchResourceName). An empty uri, or one with a "." or ".." path segment, is never allowed by restricted caveats — an operation that cannot name what it touches cannot be shown to stay inside the scope.

<sub>[resource.go](../../resource.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Caveats.Check"></a>

#### limes.Caveats.Check

```go
func (c Caveats) Check(req CheckRequest) error
```

Check evaluates every per-operation caveat against req and returns the first violation, as one of the sentinels above, or nil. A declared Effect that Op.ResolveEffect refuses returns ErrEffectConflict, which is a programming error rather than a caveat violation. It is the one definition of what the caveats mean at use time; a consumer that hand-rolls the same checks drifts from it.

The source-IP caveat is per connection rather than per operation, so it is checked separately by CheckSource. Budget and request-count caveats are stateful and enforced by the meter (package meter).

<sub>[check.go](../../check.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Caveats.CheckSource"></a>

#### limes.Caveats.CheckSource

```go
func (c Caveats) CheckSource(addr netip.Addr) error
```

CheckSource evaluates the source-IP caveat against the client address the consumer observed, and returns ErrSourceIPNotAllowed or nil. An unknown address (the zero netip.Addr) fails a constrained capability closed: "we could not tell" is not "it matched".

<sub>[check.go](../../check.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Caveats.RestrictsResources"></a>

#### limes.Caveats.RestrictsResources

```go
func (c Caveats) RestrictsResources() bool
```

RestrictsResources reports whether the caveats confine the capability to a set of resources. False means "any resource within the tenant".

<sub>[resource.go](../../resource.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Caveats.Validate"></a>

#### limes.Caveats.Validate

```go
func (c Caveats) Validate() error
```

Validate reports whether the caveat bag is well formed. The issuer runs it before minting anything, root or delegated, so every signed capability carries caveats with one meaning. Every error matches ErrInvalidCaveats.

<sub>[validate.go](../../validate.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CheckRequest"></a>

### limes.CheckRequest

```go
type CheckRequest struct {
	// Op is the operation being performed.
	Op Op
	// Effect is what Op does to state, as the server declares it. Leave it
	// EffectUnspecified for a built-in operation; see Op.ResolveEffect.
	Effect Effect
	// Resource is the URI the operation touches. Leave it empty only for an
	// operation that is not bound to one resource; a resource-restricted
	// capability refuses such an operation (see Caveats.AllowsResource).
	// For an operation over a set — a listing, a batch — pass the URI or
	// prefix that bounds the whole set.
	Resource string
	// HasIdempotencyKey reports whether the request carried an idempotency
	// key. Consulted only when the caveats require one for a mutating
	// operation.
	HasIdempotencyKey bool
	// ResourceTainted reports whether the consumer has flagged the resource
	// with a prompt-injection / PII / secrets signal. A consumer with no
	// taint tracking leaves it false — AllowTaintedRead then protects
	// nothing, which is the consumer's to disclose.
	ResourceTainted bool
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

CheckRequest describes one operation a bearer is attempting, in the terms the caveats are written in. The consumer fills it from its own request.

<sub>[check.go](../../check.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CheckRequest.Mutating"></a>

#### limes.CheckRequest.Mutating

```go
func (req CheckRequest) Mutating() (bool, error)
```

Mutating reports whether the operation may change state, resolving its declared Effect; a declaration Op.ResolveEffect refuses is ErrEffectConflict. A consumer that gates anything else on the operation's effect — a lookup it runs only for reads — asks here, so that it and Check cannot disagree.

<sub>[check.go](../../check.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CopyCeiling"></a>

### limes.CopyCeiling

```go
type CopyCeiling struct {
	// RevocationID is the block's revocation id.
	RevocationID []byte
	// Requests bounds the requests made with the copy; nil when the block
	// set no request limit of its own. Never Unlimited: a copy only narrows.
	Requests *RequestCeiling
	// Budget bounds the copy's spend, in the capability's unit, which its
	// UnitCode carries; nil when the block set no budget of its own. Never
	// Unlimited.
	Budget *BudgetCeiling
}
```

CopyCeiling is a limit one attenuation block of a Biscuit set on the copy it ends and every copy attenuated from it, all of which carry the block's revocation id. Its counters are keyed by that id, so siblings attenuated apart count apart, while the capability's own counters still bound them all together.

```go

```

AdmitsBudget reports whether amount spent with the copy in all stays within its own budget; with none of its own, any amount does.

#### limes.CopyCeiling.AdmitsRequests

```go

```

AdmitsRequests reports whether n requests made with the copy in all stay within its own request limit; with none of its own, any number does.

<sub>[types.go](../../types.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.CopyQuota"></a>

### limes.CopyQuota

```go
type CopyQuota struct {
	// Max is the most copies counted; 0 counts none, so a copy with limits
	// of its own is refused. Within 0..MaxIJSONInteger, and 0 when
	// Unlimited.
	Max int64
	// Unlimited lifts the quota to the store's bound.
	Unlimited bool
}
```

CopyQuota bounds how many Biscuit copies of a capability a meter counts — the copies that carry limits of their own, each a counter it keeps: at most Max, or as many as the store allows when Unlimited. It counts the copies of the capability and of every capability delegated from it, as its request and budget ceilings count theirs, so a delegated child does not multiply them, and goes on counting them once a child's usage is dropped. A store counts no more than its own bound per capability either (meter.DefaultMaxCopiesPerCapability), whatever the quota.

<a id="limes.Effect"></a>

### limes.Effect

```go
type Effect uint8
```

Effect is what an operation does to state. Check uses it twice: a mutating operation may need an idempotency key (Caveats.IdempotencyKeyRequired), and a read may be refused on a tainted resource (Caveats.AllowTaintedRead).

The server that performs the operation declares the effect, from the same place it defines the operation (a method option, a tool registry), and never from anything the bearer sends.

<sub>[effect.go](../../effect.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.EffectUnspecified"></a><a id="limes.EffectRead"></a><a id="limes.EffectWrite"></a>

#### limes.EffectUnspecified, limes.EffectRead, limes.EffectWrite

```go
const (
	// EffectUnspecified takes the operation's default: the fixed effect of a
	// built-in operation, and EffectWrite for a consumer-defined one, whose
	// effect this package cannot know — so an undeclared operation errs
	// towards the caveats that tighten mutations. It errs away from the one
	// that tightens reads: a tainted resource is refused only to a read, so
	// a consumer-defined operation that reads and is left undeclared is
	// never held to AllowTaintedRead. Declare EffectRead for one.
	EffectUnspecified Effect = iota
	// EffectRead leaves state unchanged.
	EffectRead
	// EffectWrite may change state.
	EffectWrite
)
```

<sub>[effect.go](../../effect.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Effect.String"></a>

#### limes.Effect.String

```go
func (e Effect) String() string
```

String names the effect for logs and errors.

```go
func (e Effect) Validate() error
```

<a id="limes.MeterSubject"></a>

### limes.MeterSubject

```go
type MeterSubject struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

MeterSubject is what a meter.Meter counts a request against: a verified capability's id and tenant, its request and budget ceilings, its unit and the limits of the Biscuit copy presented. Only VerifiedCapability.MeterSubject and StoredMeterSubject make one, so a ceiling is the one a verified token carries or a RecordReader reads back — never a value a caller sets on the subject itself. A store reads it through its methods. The zero MeterSubject names no capability and no tenant; a meter.Meter refuses it with ErrInvalidRequest rather than count it anywhere.

<sub>[meter_subject.go](../../meter_subject.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.StoredMeterSubject"></a>

#### limes.StoredMeterSubject

```go
func StoredMeterSubject(ctx context.Context, records RecordReader, capabilityID uuid.UUID) (MeterSubject, error)
```

StoredMeterSubject is what a meter.Meter counts a capability against for a cost reported with no token in hand, read from the capability's record — records is the Store, or anything reading its records. It reads the record itself rather than take a Record, whose fields any caller can set, so the ceilings are the ones on record. A stored record names no Biscuit copy, so the subject carries none. A revoked capability still gives one: a cost already incurred belongs in the ledger. ErrNotFound when the capability is not on record.

<a id="limes.Nanos"></a>

### limes.Nanos

```go
type Nanos int64
```

Nanos is an amount of a currency or metering unit (see BudgetCeiling.UnitCode) in billionths of the unit: 1.5 USD is 1\_500\_000\_000. Every amount the module counts — a charge, a ceiling, a hold, a refund — is Nanos, so spend sums, compares and refunds exactly, however many charges it takes. Float64 appears only at the edges, for display (Float64) and for a caller whose prices arrive as floats (AmountFromFloat).

In JSON, and so in a capability token, an amount is a decimal number of units in a string ("max\_budget": "1.5"), written and read without a float64 in between.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MaxNanos"></a>

#### limes.MaxNanos

```go
const MaxNanos Nanos = 999_999_999_999_999_999
```

MaxNanos is the largest amount the module counts: just under a billion units, which is what a column of numeric(18,9) holds. Bounding every amount and counter by it leaves the sum of any two inside int64.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.AmountFromFloat"></a>

#### limes.AmountFromFloat

```go
func AmountFromFloat(f float64) (Nanos, error)
```

AmountFromFloat converts an amount held as a float64 to Nanos, rounding to the nearest nano, halves to even. It reads the float as the shortest decimal that identifies it — 0.1 as "0.1", the sum 0.1+0.2 as "0.30000000000000004" — so an amount written with at most nine decimals and fifteen significant digits converts exactly. It refuses what Nanos.Validate refuses, and NaN and the infinities.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MustParseAmount"></a>

#### limes.MustParseAmount

```go
func MustParseAmount(s string) Nanos
```

MustParseAmount is ParseAmount for an amount written into the program, a price or a test value: it panics on one ParseAmount refuses.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ParseAmount"></a>

#### limes.ParseAmount

```go
func ParseAmount(s string) (Nanos, error)
```

ParseAmount reads a decimal amount of units — "0.35", "25", "1e-7" — into Nanos exactly. It refuses, as ErrInvalidAmount, a negative amount, one finer than a nano and one beyond MaxNanos, rather than rounding any of them, and text that is not digits with an optional fraction and an optional exponent of at most three digits.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.Float64"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.Float64

```go
func (n Nanos) Float64() float64
```

Float64 is n in units, the nearest float64. For display and metrics only: never count with it.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.MarshalJSON"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.MarshalJSON

```go
func (n Nanos) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalJSON writes n as a JSON string holding a decimal number of units, "1.5": a string, so that a reader whose numbers are float64 — JavaScript's JSON.parse among them — cannot round it.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.MarshalText"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.MarshalText

```go
func (n Nanos) MarshalText() ([]byte, error)
```

MarshalText writes n as a decimal number of units, as String does.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.String"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.String

```go
func (n Nanos) String() string
```

String writes n as a decimal number of units with no trailing zeros: "1.5", "0.000000001", "25".

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.UnmarshalJSON"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.UnmarshalJSON

```go
func (n *Nanos) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error
```

UnmarshalJSON reads what MarshalJSON writes, exactly, as ParseAmount does: a JSON string, never a number.

<sub>[nanos.go](../../nanos.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Nanos.UnmarshalText"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.UnmarshalText

```go
func (n *Nanos) UnmarshalText(b []byte) error
```

UnmarshalText reads a decimal number of units exactly, as ParseAmount does: configuration that carries an amount — a YAML scalar, an environment variable — reads it without a float64 in between.

<a id="limes.Nanos.Validate"></a>

#### limes.Nanos.Validate

```go

```

Validate reports whether n is usable as a charge or refund amount: not negative and at most MaxNanos, else ErrInvalidAmount. Implementations call it before touching state.

<a id="limes.Op"></a>

### limes.Op

```go
type Op string
```

Op is an operation an agent may perform. The package defines a small built-in set (below); a consumer adds its own as namespaced names of the form "\<namespace>:\<name>" — "tool:search", "mcp:github/create\_issue" — which Op.Validate accepts. A consumer-defined operation is treated as state-changing unless the server declares otherwise (Effect).

<sub>[types.go](../../types.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.OpGet"></a><a id="limes.OpPut"></a><a id="limes.OpList"></a><a id="limes.OpDelete"></a><a id="limes.OpShare"></a><a id="limes.OpManage"></a>

#### limes.OpGet, limes.OpPut, limes.OpList, limes.OpDelete, limes.OpShare, limes.OpManage

```go
const (
	OpGet    Op = "get"    // read one resource
	OpPut    Op = "put"    // write one resource
	OpList   Op = "list"   // list resources under a prefix
	OpDelete Op = "delete" // delete a resource
	OpShare  Op = "share"  // delegate a sub-capability to another agent through the issuer; not needed to attenuate a Biscuit copy
	OpManage Op = "manage" // administer: tenants, policy
)
```

The built-in operations: the ones every resource server shares. Get and List read; the rest may change state (Op.ResolveEffect). A domain's own operations — searching an index, computing embeddings — are the consumer's, namespaced: "index:search", "model:embed".

<sub>[types.go](../../types.go)</sub>

#### limes.Op.Builtin

```go

```

Builtin reports whether op is one of the operations this package defines.

<a id="limes.Op.ResolveEffect"></a>

#### limes.Op.ResolveEffect

```go
func (op Op) ResolveEffect(declared Effect) (Effect, error)
```

ResolveEffect returns the effect Check applies to op, given the effect the consumer declared for it. A built-in operation keeps its own effect, and a declaration may only repeat it; a consumer-defined operation takes the declaration, or EffectWrite when there is none. An effect this package does not define, or one contradicting a built-in operation's, is ErrEffectConflict.

#### limes.Op.Validate

```go
func (op Op) Validate() error
```

Validate reports whether op is well formed: a built-in operation, or a namespaced one of the form "\<namespace>:\<name>" made of printable, non-space ASCII. Every error matches ErrInvalidCaveats.

<a id="limes.Principal"></a>

### limes.Principal

```go
type Principal struct {
	// Type discriminates the principal kind.
	Type PrincipalType
	// TenantID is required for every principal — capability without
	// tenant scope is malformed and the verifier rejects it.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Subject is the stable identity (user UUID, agent run ID, service
	// account name). Format depends on Type.
	Subject string
	// Agent fields are populated only for Type == PrincipalTypeAgent.
	Agent *AgentPrincipal
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Principal identifies the subject the capability is issued to. It is written into a token as the limes\_principal claim (wire.go). Agent principals have a richer shape than service principals: they carry the run / tool-call lineage that audit and cost attribution need.

<sub>[principal.go](../../principal.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Principal.Clone"></a>

```go
func (p Principal) Clone() Principal
```

Clone is p with agent details of its own: a store keeps, and hands out, a principal no caller can alter through a pointer it kept.

<a id="limes.Principal.Validate"></a>

#### limes.Principal.Validate

```go
func (p Principal) Validate() error
```

Validate reports whether p names a principal a capability can be issued to: one of the principal kinds, spelled as the constants spell it, and agent details only on an agent. The kind is part of the token, so a kind outside the set would be signed and then read by every verifier as it pleased. Its subject and agent details are text a store keeps: valid UTF-8 without NUL (docs/compatibility.md).
